column1: # scripts/corpus-floors.tsv — the tracked minimum size of every gated enumeration.
# A gate that enumerates a corpus, a fixture set, a symbol list or a test set
# and then compares or asserts over it proves NOTHING when the enumeration is
# empty: two empty sets are identical, an empty loop counts zero failures, and
# the gate exits 0 forever. A corpus that silently shrinks from 57 fixtures to
# 3 is the same defect in slower motion.
# Every such gate declares its size here and asserts it through
# scripts/lib/corpus-floor.sh (shell) or scripts/lib/corpus_floor.py (Python).
# scripts/check-corpus-floors.sh proves every row still has a live call site,
# so a floor cannot be retired by deleting the assertion that reads it.
# Columns (tab-separated):
#   key          the assertion key, referenced by exactly one call site
#   mode         exact — curated, stable corpus: ANY change fails, up or down
#                min   — legitimately grows: below `floor` fails, and so does
#                        anything above floor+slack (an unraised floor stops
#                        being a floor)
#   floor        expected count (exact) or tracked minimum (min)
#   slack        how far above `floor` a min corpus may drift before the gate
#                asks for the floor to be raised; `-` for exact rows
#   description  what is being counted
# MAINTENANCE: the counts live in the same commit as the corpus. Add fixtures,
# the gate goes red and names this file and the new number; edit the row in
# that same commit. Remove fixtures, the gate goes red and asks you to justify
# the smaller number in the commit body. There is no path where the count
# drifts without somebody saying so out loud.
# key
corpus-floor-registry
column5: rows in this registry, asserted by scripts/check-corpus-floors.sh
